content:
The image shows a green leaf with white, powdery patches scattered across the upper surface. The coating has a dusty, flour-like texture typical of fungal sporulation directly on the leaf surface. There is no necrosis, water-soaking, yellowing, or lesion borders — just the white powdery growth on otherwise green tissue.

This pattern is the hallmark of **Powdery Mildew**: superficial white mycelium and conidia forming on the leaf epidermis, appearing as discrete to coalescing powdery white spots.
